 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Your Kansas State Wildcats played their most complete game of the season on Monday in an 86-45 rout of visiting Montana to move to 3-1 on the season. The Cats had more steals (9) than turnovers (8), and did a significant portion of their damage in the paint against the under-sized Grizzlies — showing that Casey Alexander's squad doesn't have to live behind the arc to win games.
 Now it's time to see if K-State can put together a couple of games of good defense. The theme so far of the season has been to get better every game, and the better that would be good to see tonight is a second-straight quality defensive effort. And they'll be tested by a Campbell squad that is good at scoring in bunches.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Camels enter tonight at just 1-4 on the season, but all four losses have come away from home, and just two days ago they held a 47-43 lead over Oklahoma at halftime before running out of steam down the stretch. They are led in scoring by sophomore guard Rashawn Inglemon, who was the SAC Freshman of the Year last season at D-II Anderson University. They will get a lot of rebounds, but they don't force a lot of turnovers — something that should benefit the Cats. For a full breakdown of the Camels, be sure and check out Drew's post .
 If the Cats can continue to show improvement, this should be a tough be easily winnable game. But they'll need to play 40 minutes, because Campbell can get just as hot in the second half as the first (just ask NC State). Time to go out there an finish up this homestand strong, focus on tonight, and keep building momentum before facing Gonzaga next week.
 We've got an 7:01pm CT tipoff from Bramlage Colisuem, and you can catch the action on ESPN+ with Ben Boyle (play-by-play), Stan Weber (analyst), and Addison Love (sideline reporter) on the call.
 If you can't access the stream, the game can be heard across portions of the 29-station K-State Sports Network with Wyatt Thompson (play-by-play) and Matt Walters (analyst) calling the action. The game will also be available online at K-Statesports.com and via the Varsity Network app, and on satellite radio at Sirius 270. Live stats are also available at k-statesports.com, and social media updates (@KStateMBB) will also be a part of the coverage.
